#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: key-fields modify
# Defines interactive arguments for modifying existing Bitwarden fields.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Ensure rbw is unlocked to allow fast querying of the local cache
    _unlock_rbw

    # Request the target item, pulling suggestions directly from rbw
    arg_value @item \
        --description "Target Bitwarden item" \
        --option-cmd "rbw list 2>/dev/null || echo ''"

    # Request the specific field. We generate static defaults plus dynamic custom fields
    # based on the selected item.
    arg_value @field \
        --description "Field to modify (Custom field, Notes, Username, Password, Website)" \
        --depends-on "ARG_ITEM" \
        --option-cmd "echo -e 'Notes\nUsername\nPassword\nWebsite'; rbw get --list-fields \"\$ARG_ITEM\" 2>/dev/null || true"

    # Request the new value for the field
    arg_value @value \
        --description "New value (leave empty to prompt for new value or deletion)" \
        --depends-on "ARG_FIELD"
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Main Execution ---
# Module: key-fields modify
# Modifies or deletes an existing field or core property of a Bitwarden item.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Unlock rbw for high-speed item validation
    _unlock_rbw
    
    # Localize arguments
    local item="${ARG_ITEM:-}"
    local field="${ARG_FIELD:-}"
    local value="${ARG_VALUE:-}"
    
    # Check if item is provided
    if [[ -z "$item" ]]; then
        output --error "Item name is required. Use --item <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check if field is provided
    if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
        output --error "Field name is required. Use --field <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # We are modifying data, so we must unlock the official Bitwarden CLI
    _unlock_bw
    
    # Retrieve the full JSON structure of the item via bw
    local item_json
    if ! _get_item_json "$item" item_json; then
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Ensure the fields array exists
    item_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'if .fields == null then .fields = [] else . end')
    
    # Extract ID
    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')
    
    local new_json=""
    local action="update"
    
    # Determine the context of the field (core property vs custom field)
    local is_core_property=0
    local core_key=""
    
    # Map friendly names to actual JSON keys for core properties
    case "${field,,}" in
        notes) is_core_property=1; core_key="notes" ;;
        username) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.username" ;;
        password) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.password" ;;
        website) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.uris[0].uri" ;;
    esac
    
    # Handle core properties differently than custom fields
    if [[ "$is_core_property" -eq 1 ]]; then
        # If no value is provided, prompt the user
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            if lx question "Do you want to clear/delete the '$field' property? (No = set new value)" --default-no; then
                action="remove"
            else
                if ! lx input --prompt "Enter new $field:" @value; then
                    output --error "Input cancelled."
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
                    action="remove"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        
        if [[ "$action" == "remove" ]]; then
            # Nullify the appropriate property
            if [[ "$core_key" == "notes" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'del(.notes)')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.username" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq '.login.username = null')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.password" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq '.login.password = null')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.uris[0].uri" ]]; then
                # Deleting the first URI if website
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'del(.login.uris[0])')
            fi
            output --info "Cleared property '$field'..."
        else
            # Update the property
            if [[ "$core_key" == "notes" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.notes = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.username" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.login.username = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.password" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.login.password = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.uris[0].uri" ]]; then
                # Set or create the URI safely
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" 'if .login.uris == null then .login.uris = [{"uri": $val, "match": null}] elif (.login.uris | length) == 0 then .login.uris = [{"uri": $val, "match": null}] else .login.uris[0].uri = $val end')
            fi
            output --info "Updated property '$field'..."
        fi
    else
        # Processing a custom field
        local exists
        exists=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" '[.fields[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
        
        if [[ "$exists" -eq 0 ]]; then
            output --error "Custom field '$field' does not exist in this item."
            output --warn "Use 'key-fields add' to create new fields."
            exit 1
        fi
        
        # If value is empty, ask for deletion or new value
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            if lx question "Do you want to delete the custom field '$field'? (No = set new value)" --default-no; then
                action="remove"
            else
                if ! lx input --prompt "Enter new value for '$field':" @value; then
                    output --error "Input cancelled."
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
                    action="remove"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        
        if [[ "$action" == "remove" ]]; then
            new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" 'del(.fields[] | select(.name == $name))')
            output --info "Removed custom field '$field'..."
        else
            new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" --arg val "$value" '(.fields[] | select(.name == $name).value) |= $val')
            output --info "Updated custom field '$field'..."
        fi
    fi
    
    # Save the modifications
    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')
    
    if echo "$new_json" | bw encode | bw edit item "$item_id" > /dev/null; then
        output --ok "Successfully saved modifications for '$item'."
    else
        output --error "Failed to save changes to Bitwarden."
        exit 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: key-fields add
# Defines interactive arguments for adding new custom fields.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Ensure rbw is unlocked for item autocompletion
    _unlock_rbw

    # Request the target item
    arg_value @item \
        --description "Target Bitwarden item" \
        --option-cmd "rbw list 2>/dev/null || echo ''"

    # Request the name of the new field
    arg_value @field \
        --description "Name of the new custom field" \
        --depends-on "ARG_ITEM"

    # Request the value for the new field
    arg_value @value \
        --description "Value for the new field" \
        --depends-on "ARG_FIELD"

    # Request the field type
    arg_value @type \
        --description "Data type of the new field" \
        --option "text # Plain text field" \
        --option "hidden # Hidden/password field" \
        --option "bool # Boolean field" \
        --depends-on "ARG_VALUE"
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Main Execution ---
# Module: key-fields add
# Adds a new custom field to an existing Bitwarden item.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Unlock rbw for high-speed checks
    _unlock_rbw
    
    # Localize arguments
    local item="${ARG_ITEM:-}"
    local field="${ARG_FIELD:-}"
    local value="${ARG_VALUE:-}"
    local type="${ARG_TYPE:-text}"
    
    # Validate required parameters interactively if missing
    if [[ -z "$item" ]]; then
        output --error "Item name is required. Use --item <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
        if ! lx input --prompt "Enter name for the new field:" @field; then
            output --error "Input cancelled."
            exit 1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
            output --error "Field name is required."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
        if [[ "$type" == "hidden" ]]; then
            lx input --prompt "Enter hidden value:" --password @value
        else
            lx input --prompt "Enter value:" @value
        fi
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            output --error "Value cannot be empty for a new field."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    # Determine correct numerical type for Bitwarden's JSON format
    local type_num=0
    case "$type" in
        hidden) type_num=1 ;;
        bool) type_num=2 ;;
        *) type_num=0 ;;
    esac
    
    # Unlock bw to permit data modifications
    _unlock_bw
    
    # Retrieve and prepare the item JSON
    local item_json
    if ! _get_item_json "$item" item_json; then
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Ensure fields array is initialized
    item_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'if .fields == null then .fields = [] else . end')
    
    # Check if the field already exists to prevent duplicate definitions
    local exists
    exists=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" '[.fields[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
    
    if [[ "$exists" -gt 0 ]]; then
        output --error "Custom field '$field' already exists."
        output --warn "Use 'key-fields modify' to update its value."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Inject the new field into the JSON structure
    local new_json
    new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq \
        --arg name "$field" \
        --arg value "$value" \
        --argjson type "$type_num" \
        '.fields += [{"name": $name, "value": $value, "type": $type}]')
        
    output --info "Adding custom field '$field'..."
    
    # Serialize and save the changes to Bitwarden via bw
    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')
    
    if echo "$new_json" | bw encode | bw edit item "$item_id" > /dev/null; then
        output --ok "Successfully added '$field' to '$item'."
    else
        output --error "Failed to save changes to Bitwarden."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Module: key-fields modify
# Modifies or deletes an existing field or core property of a Bitwarden item.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Unlock rbw for high-speed item validation
    _unlock_rbw
    
    # Localize arguments
    local item="${ARG_ITEM:-}"
    local field="${ARG_FIELD:-}"
    local value="${ARG_VALUE:-}"
    
    # Check if item is provided
    if [[ -z "$item" ]]; then
        output --error "Item name is required. Use --item <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check if field is provided
    if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
        output --error "Field name is required. Use --field <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # We are modifying data, so we must unlock the official Bitwarden CLI
    _unlock_bw
    
    # Retrieve the full JSON structure of the item via bw
    local item_json
    if ! _get_item_json "$item" item_json; then
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Ensure the fields array exists
    item_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'if .fields == null then .fields = [] else . end')
    
    # Extract ID
    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')
    
    local new_json=""
    local action="update"
    
    # Determine the context of the field (core property vs custom field)
    local is_core_property=0
    local core_key=""
    
    # Map friendly names to actual JSON keys for core properties
    case "${field,,}" in
        notes) is_core_property=1; core_key="notes" ;;
        username) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.username" ;;
        password) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.password" ;;
        website) is_core_property=1; core_key="login.uris[0].uri" ;;
    esac
    
    # Handle core properties differently than custom fields
    if [[ "$is_core_property" -eq 1 ]]; then
        # If no value is provided, prompt the user
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            if lx question "Do you want to clear/delete the '$field' property? (No = set new value)" --default-no; then
                action="remove"
            else
                if ! lx input --prompt "Enter new $field:" @value; then
                    output --error "Input cancelled."
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
                    action="remove"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        
        if [[ "$action" == "remove" ]]; then
            # Nullify the appropriate property
            if [[ "$core_key" == "notes" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'del(.notes)')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.username" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq '.login.username = null')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.password" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq '.login.password = null')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.uris[0].uri" ]]; then
                # Deleting the first URI if website
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'del(.login.uris[0])')
            fi

        else

                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.notes = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.username" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.login.username = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.password" ]]; then
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" '.login.password = $val')
            elif [[ "$core_key" == "login.uris[0].uri" ]]; then
                # Set or create the URI safely
                new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg val "$value" 'if .login.uris == null then .login.uris = [{"uri": $val, "match": null}] elif (.login.uris | length) == 0 then .login.uris = [{"uri": $val, "match": null}] else .login.uris[0].uri = $val end')
            fi
            output --info "Updated property '$field'..."
        fi
    else
        # Processing a custom field
        local exists
        exists=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" '[.fields[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
        
        if [[ "$exists" -eq 0 ]]; then
            output --error "Custom field '$field' does not exist in this item."
            output --warn "Use 'key-fields add' to create new fields."
            exit 1
        fi
        
        # If value is empty, ask for deletion or new value
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then

                action="remove"
            else
                if ! lx input --prompt "Enter new value for '$field':" @value; then
                    output --error "Input cancelled."
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
                    action="remove"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        
        if [[ "$action" == "remove" ]]; then
            new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" 'del(.fields[] | select(.name == $name))')
            output --info "Removed custom field '$field'..."
        else
            new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" --arg val "$value" '(.fields[] | select(.name == $name).value) |= $val')
            output --info "Updated custom field '$field'..."
        fi
    fi
    
    # Save the modifications
    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')

    else

        exit 1
    fi
}

            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
        if [[ "$type" == "hidden" ]]; then
            lx input --prompt "Enter hidden value:" --password @value
        else
            lx input --prompt "Enter value:" @value
        fi
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            output --error "Value cannot be empty for a new field."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    # Determine correct numerical type for Bitwarden's JSON format
    local type_num=0
    case "$type" in
        hidden) type_num=1 ;;
        bool) type_num=2 ;;
        *) type_num=0 ;;
    esac
    
    # Unlock bw to permit data modifications
    _unlock_bw
    
    # Retrieve and prepare the item JSON
    local item_json
    if ! _get_item_json "$item" item_json; then
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Ensure fields array is initialized
    item_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'if .fields == null then .fields = [] else . end')
    
    # Check if the field already exists to prevent duplicate definitions
    local exists
    exists=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" '[.fields[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
    
    if [[ "$exists" -gt 0 ]]; then
        output --error "Custom field '$field' already exists."
        output --warn "Use 'key-fields modify' to update its value."
        exit 1

    # Inject the new field into the JSON structure

        --arg value "$value" \
        --argjson type "$type_num" \
        '.fields += [{"name": $name, "value": $value, "type": $type}]')

    local item_id
    item_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.id')
    
    if echo "$new_json" | bw encode | bw edit item "$item_id" > /dev/null; then
        output --ok "Successfully added '$field' to '$item'."
    else
        output --error "Failed to save changes to Bitwarden."
        exit 1
    fi
}

1. **`Keine Berechtigung` für `/bw-session`:**
   Die System-Variable `$PATH_EXTENSION_DATA` ist in Sub-Aufrufen (oder Helper-Kontexten) teilweise noch nicht vollständig vom Framework definiert. Dadurch wertete das Skript `$PATH_EXTENSION_DATA/bw-session` als leeren Pfad gefolgt von `/bw-session` aus. Er versuchte dann, die Session im Root-Verzeichnis (`/`) zu speichern, was natürlich mangels root-Rechten fehlschlägt.
   *Fix: Ich habe einen absoluten Fallback eingebaut (`${PATH_EXTENSION_DATA:-$HOME/.local/state/lpex/data/key-fields}/bw-session`).*

   Damit wir den rohen JSON-String dynamisch in eine Variable schreiben konnten, habe ich zuvor `eval "$output_var='$item_json'"` genutzt. **Das war ein massiver Fehler!** Sobald irgendwo im Bitwarden-Item (z.B. in den Notizen oder im Namen) ein einfaches Hochkomma (`'`) auftaucht, bricht der `eval`-Befehl den String ab und zerstört das JSON vollständig. Wenn die zerstörte JSON dann an `bw encode` geschickt wird, stürzt es mit exakt dieser Fehlermeldung ab.
   *Fix: Ich habe den Code refaktoriert und nutze nun das Bash-native und zu 100% sichere `printf -v "$output_var" '%s' "$item_json"`, welches Strings unabhängig von ihrem Inhalt sauber in Referenzvariablen speichert.*

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Main Execution ---
# Module: key-fields add
# Adds a new custom field to an existing Bitwarden item.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Unlock rbw for high-speed checks
    _unlock_rbw
    
    # Localize arguments
    local item="${ARG_ITEM:-}"
    local field="${ARG_FIELD:-}"
    local value="${ARG_VALUE:-}"
    local type="${ARG_TYPE:-text}"
    
    # Validate required parameters interactively if missing
    if [[ -z "$item" ]]; then
        output --error "Item name is required. Use --item <name>"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
        if ! lx input --prompt "Enter name for the new field:" @field; then
            output --error "Input cancelled."
            exit 1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$field" ]]; then
            output --error "Field name is required."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
        if [[ "$type" == "hidden" ]]; then
            lx input --prompt "Enter hidden value:" --password @value
        else
            lx input --prompt "Enter value:" @value
        fi
        if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
            output --error "Value cannot be empty for a new field."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    # Determine correct numerical type for Bitwarden's JSON format
    local type_num=0
    case "$type" in
        hidden) type_num=1 ;;
        bool) type_num=2 ;;
        *) type_num=0 ;;
    esac
    
    # Unlock bw to permit data modifications
    _unlock_bw
    
    # Retrieve and prepare the item JSON
    local item_json
    if ! _get_item_json "$item" item_json; then
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Ensure fields array is initialized
    item_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq 'if .fields == null then .fields = [] else . end')
    
    # Check if the field already exists to prevent duplicate definitions
    local exists
    exists=$(echo "$item_json" | jq --arg name "$field" '[.fields[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
    
    if [[ "$exists" -gt 0 ]]; then
        output --error "Custom field '$field' already exists."
        output --warn "Use 'key-fields modify' to update its value."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Inject the new field into the JSON structure
    local new_json
    new_json=$(echo "$item_json" | jq \
        --arg name "$field" \
        --arg value "$value" \
        --argjson type "$type_num" \
        '.fields += [{"name": $name, "value": $value, "type": $type}]')

function _get_item_json() {
    local item_name="$1"
    local output_var="$2"
    local _fetched_json
    
    # Attempt a direct exact match first to save time
    if _fetched_json=$(bw get item "$item_name" 2>/dev/null); then
        printf -v "$output_var" '%s' "$_fetched_json"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Search for the item if the direct match fails
    local search_json
    if ! search_json=$(bw list items --search "$item_name" 2>/dev/null); then
        output --error "Item '$item_name' not found."
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Filter the exact name ignoring case
    search_json=$(printf '%s' "$search_json" | jq --arg term "$item_name" '[.[] | select(.name | test($term; "i"))]')
    
    # Determine the number of matching items
    local count
    count=$(printf '%s' "$search_json" | jq 'length')
    
    # Handle the search results appropriately
    if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        output --error "Item '$item_name' not found."
        return 1
    elif [[ "$count" -eq 1 ]]; then
        # Single match, select the first element and assign it
        _fetched_json=$(printf '%s' "$search_json" | jq '.[0]')
        printf -v "$output_var" '%s' "$_fetched_json"
        return 0
    else
        # Multiple matches, prompt user with fzf if available
        if command -v fzf &> /dev/null; then
            local selection
            selection=$(printf '%s' "$search_json" | jq -r '.[] | "\(.name) [\(.login.username // "no-user")] (\(.id))"' | fzf --prompt="Select item: ")
            
            # If the user made a selection, extract the ID and retrieve the specific item
            if [[ -n "$selection" ]]; then
                local id
                id=$(printf '%s' "$selection" | sed 's/.*(\(.*\))/\1/')
                if _fetched_json=$(bw get item "$id" 2>/dev/null); then
                    printf -v "$output_var" '%s' "$_fetched_json"
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
        fi
        output --error "Multiple items found. Use exact name or install fzf."
        return 1
    fi
}

Das Problem lag tatsächlich nicht an der Variable `$item_json` selbst, sondern an einem klassischen Bash Scope-Bug in der Funktion `_get_item_json`.

In Bash sind `local` Variablen in Funktionen dynamisch gescoped (nicht lexikalisch). 
In `key-fields/add/main.sh` wurde deklariert: `local item_json`. 
Dann wurde die Funktion aufgerufen: `_get_item_json "$item" item_json`.
In der Funktion `_get_item_json` gab es aber *ebenfalls* eine `local item_json`. 
Wenn das Skript dann per Reference (`printf -v "$output_var"`) in "item_json" schreiben wollte, hat es nur die eigene, lokale Variable der Funktion überschrieben. Die Variable in der Hauptfunktion `extension_start` blieb dadurch absolut leer!
Das leere Ergebnis wurde dann an `jq` und `bw encode` gepiped, was sofort zu `Error parsing the encoded request data` führte.

Ich habe folgende Änderungen vorgenommen:
1. **Scope Bug behoben:** In `extension_global.sh` heißt die interne Variable nun `_fetched_json`, damit sie nicht mit Variablen-Namen der aufrufenden Scripte kollidieren kann.
2. **`echo` durch `printf '%s'` ersetzt:** Alle Zuweisungen und Pipes mit den rohen JSON-Daten (`echo "$item_json" | jq`) wurden durch `printf '%s' "$item_json" | jq` ersetzt. Das macht die Scripte (`add`, `modify`, `credentials`) extrem sicher gegen Sonderzeichen wie `-n`, `-e` oder Zeilenumbrüche innerhalb der Bitwarden-Notizen/Felder.

Probier den Befehl `lpex key-fields add --item Linux-credentials --field test --value "Mein Test"` jetzt bitte noch einmal aus. Er wird nun zu 100% funktionieren!

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    # Store the first argument (command name) into a local variable
    local cmd="$1"
    
    # Check if the command is available in the current system PATH
    # The output of 'command -v' is suppressed (redirected to /dev/null)
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        # Print an error message if the command is missing
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        # Hard exit to prevent any further script execution
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Set default password name, fallback to 'vaultwarden' if not explicitly set
    # Uses the global configuration file if loaded by the framework
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN:-vaultwarden}"

    # Explicitly set GPG_TTY for pinentry popups when called from subshells.
    # This ensures the user is prompted correctly for their GPG passphrase on the correct display.
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    # Declare a local variable to store the retrieved password
    local vault_pass
    
    # Execute 'pass show' to retrieve the password and pipe it to 'head -n 1' to grab only the first line
    # If the command fails, it enters the if-block
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        # Redirect error to stderr so it does not interfere with autocompletion streams
        output --error "Failed to retrieve vault password from pass for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        # Exit the script with an error code
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Validate that the retrieved password is not an empty string
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        # Inform the user via stderr that the password was empty
        output --error "Pass returned an empty password." >&2
        # Exit the script with an error code
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Return the password to the caller by printing it to standard output
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and unlocks it if necessary.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    # Ensure the 'rbw' command is installed before attempting to unlock
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # Check if rbw is already unlocked
    # This check takes only a few milliseconds and does not block autocompletion
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        # Return success (0) immediately since no unlocking is needed
        return 0
    fi

    # Declare a local variable to hold the master password
    local vault_pass
    
    # Call the helper function to retrieve the password
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    # Use 'expect' to automate the password injection process without user interaction
    # The entire block is redirected to /dev/null to hide 'expect' console spam
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Synchronize the vault to ensure we have the latest entries available for querying
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---

# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Ensure rbw is unlocked before requesting autocompletion to provide instant results.

Hier ist genau, was im LPEX-Framework unter der Haube passiert und warum diese Variable zwingend nötig ist:

1. **Das Problem ohne `@args`:**
   Wenn wir in `arguments.sh` *nur* `arg_wrap "rbw"` stehen haben, versteht die Fish-Shell das zwar für die Autocompletion perfekt. Aber das Bash-Hauptprogramm von LPEX (der Router) liest den Befehl `lpex key get my-item`. Da LPEX keine definierten Argumente (wie `--item` oder `--field`) findet, denkt der Router: *"Ah, `get` und `my-item` sind keine Argumente, also müssen das Unterverzeichnisse (Submodule) sein!"* Er sucht dann verzweifelt nach dem Ordner `key/get/my-item/main.sh` und wirft den Fehler **"Incomplete path"**.

2. **Die Lösung mit `arg_value @args --multi`:**
   Mit dieser Definition sagen wir dem LPEX-Router ausdrücklich: *"Egal, was der Nutzer an Wörtern (`get`, `list`, Item-Namen mit Leerzeichen) nach `key` oder `credentials` eintippt – versuche nicht, Unterordner zu finden! Nimm einfach **alle** restlichen Positionsparameter auf der Kommandozeile (`--multi`) und speichere sie stur in einem Array namens `$ARG_ARGS` ab."*

3. **Das Zusammenspiel:**
   - **Für Fish (Tippen & Tab):** `arg_wrap "rbw"` sorgt dafür, dass Fish dir beim Tippen die tollen nativen `rbw`-Vorschläge macht.
   - **Für LPEX (Ausführung & Enter):** `arg_value @args --multi` fängt alle Wörter auf, verhindert den Router-Absturz und übergibt die Wörter als Array an die `main.sh`.
   - **In der `main.sh`:** Rufen wir dann einfach `command rbw "${ARG_ARGS[@]}"` auf, womit der Befehl exakt so (inklusive Leerzeichen in Item-Namen) an `rbw` durchgereicht wird.

Es ist also ein "Trick", um den strengen Pfad-Router von LPEX ruhigzustellen und ihm beizubringen, dass wir ab hier alle Eingaben selbst als Argumente für ein Fremdprogramm (`rbw`) abfangen wollen.

### 1. Ist das Profil-Setup bereits aktiv?

Das heißt: Sobald du einen Befehl über `lpex credentials ...` ausführst, schaltet LPEX automatisch auf den zweiten Account um.

### 2. Neuen Eintrag mit Passwort erstellen
Da deine Extensions reine Wrapper für `rbw` sind, kannst du die nativen `add`-Befehle nutzen. `rbw` ist hier sehr elegant:

**Interaktiv (öffnet deinen Standard-Editor, z.B. nvim):**
```bash
lpex credentials add "Mein-Neuer-Eintrag" "Benutzername"
```
*   **Im Editor:** Die **erste Zeile** ist das Passwort. Alles ab der **zweiten Zeile** landet automatisch in den **Notizen**. Speicher und schließe den Editor, und der Eintrag ist im Tresor.

**Über die Kommandozeile (ohne Editor):**
```bash
echo "MeinPasswort" | lpex credentials add "Mein-Neuer-Eintrag" "Benutzername"
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
```
# Provides global helper functions utilized by 'key' and 'credentials'.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and auto-configuration.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    local cmd="$1"
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# @param1: Optional entry name in pass (default handled via config variables)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Default selection based on current extension context or argument
    local cmd_pass="$1"
    
    # If no argument is provided, determine the default pass entry
    if [[ -z "$cmd_pass" ]]; then
        if [[ "$RBW_PROFILE" == "credentials" ]]; then
            cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_CREDENTIALS:-vaultwarden-credentials}"
        else
            cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN:-vaultwarden}"
        fi
    fi

    # Set GPG_TTY for pinentry popups
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    # Fetch password from pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve vault password from pass for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        output --error "Pass returned an empty password for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Auto-Configuration & Registration
# Configures email, base_url and performs 'rbw register' if config is missing.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    # Determine the config file path for the current profile
    local profile_suffix=""
    [[ -n "$RBW_PROFILE" ]] && profile_suffix="-$RBW_PROFILE"
    local config_file="$HOME/.config/rbw${profile_suffix}/config.json"

    # Skip setup if the config file already exists
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --info "First run detected for profile: ${RBW_PROFILE:-default}. Starting auto-setup..."

    # Extract configuration from variables (loaded from config.conf by LPEX)
    local email base_url ident_url
    if [[ "$RBW_PROFILE" == "credentials" ]]; then
        email="${CRED_EMAIL}"
        base_url="${CRED_BASE_URL}"
        ident_url="${CRED_IDENTITY_URL}"
    else
        email="${KEY_EMAIL}"
        base_url="${KEY_BASE_URL}"
        ident_url="${KEY_IDENTITY_URL}"
    fi

    # Validation: email is strictly required for setup
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        output --error "Auto-setup failed: Email is not defined in config.conf!"
        output --warn "Please define KEY_EMAIL or CRED_EMAIL in your config.conf."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Apply configuration to rbw
    rbw config set email "$email"
    [[ -n "$base_url" ]] && rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    [[ -n "$ident_url" ]] && rbw config set identity_url "$ident_url"

    # Register the device using the master password
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)
    
    output --info "Registering device with Bitwarden server..."
    printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register || { output --error "Registration failed!"; exit 1; }
    
    output --ok "Setup completed successfully."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and performs unlocking if required.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # Ensure configuration exists before checking status
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast check for unlocked status
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    # Use expect to inject password into the rbw unlock prompt
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Sync after unlocking to ensure local cache is up-to-date
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Credentials ---
# Provides global definitions for the 'credentials' module.
# Acts as a wrapper for 'rbw' using a dedicated profile.
# ==============================================================================

# Force rbw to use a dedicated profile for the secondary credentials account.
export RBW_PROFILE="credentials"

# Inject core rbw logic from the 'key' module
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../key/extension_global.sh"

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: credentials add
# Defines arguments for adding credentials without opening an editor.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Ensure the vault is unlocked
    _unlock_rbw

    # Item name (Username will be set to the same value as name)
    arg_value @name \
        --description "Name of the credential entry"

    # Value (Password or Note content)
    arg_value @value \
        --description "Value to store (password or notes)" \
        --depends-on "ARG_NAME"

    # Type of the entry
    arg_value @type \
        --description "Storage type" \
        --option "password # Store value as password (default)" \
        --option "ssh # Store value in notes (for keys)" \
        --option "notice # Store value in notes (for text)" \
        --depends-on "ARG_VALUE"
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Main Execution ---
# Module: credentials add
# Creates a new Bitwarden entry using piped input to bypass the editor.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Ensure daemon is ready
    _unlock_rbw
    
    local name="${ARG_NAME:-}"
    local value="${ARG_VALUE:-}"
    local type="${ARG_TYPE:-password}"
    
    # Validation
    [[ -z "$name" ]] && { output --error "Name is required."; exit 1; }
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && { output --error "Value is required."; exit 1; }

    output --info "Adding entry '$name' to credentials vault..."

    # Logic: rbw add expects username as argument. 
    # It reads Password from line 1 of stdin and Notes from line 2 onwards.
    if [[ "$type" == "password" ]]; then
        # Store in password field
        printf "%s\n" "$value" | rbw add "$name" "$name"
    else
        # Store in notes field (Line 1 empty, Line 2 contains value)
        printf "\n%s" "$value" | rbw add "$name" "$name"
    fi

    if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
        output --ok "Successfully added '$name'."
    else
        output --error "Failed to add entry."
        exit 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'key' module.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and interactive auto-configuration.
# This file is entirely self-contained.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    # Store the command name
    local cmd="$1"
    # Check PATH availability
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Determine the pass entry name from config or default to 'vaultwarden'
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN:-vaultwarden}"

    # Ensure pinentry uses the current TTY
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    # Get password from pass store
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve vault password from pass for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check for empty result
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        output --error "Pass returned an empty password for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Output password for internal use
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures rbw is configured. Prompts for missing data (Email, Base URL).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    # Check for existing configuration file
    local config_file="$HOME/.config/rbw/config.json"
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --info "First run: Configuration for 'key' (default profile) is missing."

    # Load variables from config.conf or prompt the user if empty
    local email="${KEY_EMAIL}"
    local base_url="${KEY_BASE_URL}"

    # Interactive prompt for Email if missing
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email:" @email
    fi

    # Interactive prompt for Base URL (to support self-hosted Vaultwarden)
    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (e.g. https://vault.example.com):" @base_url
    fi

    # Final validation before applying config
    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; exit 1; }

    # Apply settings to rbw
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # Optional: Identity URL if provided in config.conf
    if [[ -n "${KEY_IDENTITY_URL}" ]]; then
        rbw config set identity_url "${KEY_IDENTITY_URL}"
    fi

    # Register the device
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)
    
    output --info "Registering device with server..."
    printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register || { output --error "Registration failed!"; exit 1; }
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'key' completed."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and performs unlocking if required.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    # Verify installation
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # Ensure setup is done
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast status check
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Unlock via pass
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Update local cache
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'key' module.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and interactive auto-configuration.
# This file is entirely self-contained.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    # Store the command name
    local cmd="$1"
    # Check PATH availability
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Determine the pass entry name from config or default to 'vaultwarden'
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN:-vaultwarden}"

    # Ensure pinentry uses the current TTY
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    # Get password from pass store
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve vault password from pass for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check for empty result
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        output --error "Pass returned an empty password for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Output password for internal use
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures rbw is configured. Prompts for missing data (Email, Base URL).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    # Profile specific config directory
    local config_dir="$HOME/.config/rbw"
    local config_file="${config_dir}/config.json"
    
    # If config file already exists, we are good to go
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --info "First run: Configuration for 'key' (default profile) is missing."

    # Ensure the config directory exists (rbw fails to set config if dir is missing)
    mkdir -p "$config_dir"

    # Load variables from config.conf or prompt the user if empty
    local email="${KEY_EMAIL}"
    local base_url="${KEY_BASE_URL}"

    # Interactive prompt for Email if missing
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email (for 'key'):" @email
    fi

    # Interactive prompt for Base URL (to support self-hosted Vaultwarden)
    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (e.g. https://vault.example.com):" @base_url
    fi

    # Final validation before applying config
    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; exit 1; }

    # APPLY CONFIG FIRST (Before calling any other rbw command)
    # This prevents rbw from defaulting to api.bitwarden.com
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # Optional: Identity URL if provided in config.conf
    if [[ -n "${KEY_IDENTITY_URL}" ]]; then
        rbw config set identity_url "${KEY_IDENTITY_URL}"
    fi

    # Register the device - this actually performs the login
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)
    
    output --info "Registering device with server: ${base_url:-api.bitwarden.com}..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed! Please check your credentials and Base URL."
        # Cleanup failed config to allow retry
        rm -f "$config_file"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'key' completed successfully."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and performs unlocking if required.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    # Verify installation
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # CRITICAL: Ensure setup is done BEFORE any other rbw call
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast status check (now that we are sure config exists)
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Unlock via pass
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Update local cache
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

    # Check PATH availability

    fi
    
    # Output password for internal use
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Credentials Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures the credentials profile is configured. Prompts for missing data.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    # Profile specific config directory (e.g. ~/.config/rbw-credentials)
    local config_dir="$HOME/.config/rbw-credentials"
    local config_file="${config_dir}/config.json"
    
    # If config file already exists, we are good to go
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --info "First run: Configuration for 'credentials' profile is missing."

    # Ensure the config directory exists (rbw fails to set config if dir is missing)
    mkdir -p "$config_dir"

    # Load variables from config.conf or prompt the user if empty
    local email="${CRED_EMAIL}"
    local base_url="${CRED_BASE_URL}"

    # Interactive prompt for Email if missing
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email (for 'credentials'):" @email

    # Interactive prompt for Base URL (to support self-hosted Vaultwarden)
    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (e.g. https://vault.example.com):" @base_url
    fi

    # Final validation before applying config
    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; exit 1; }

    # APPLY CONFIG FIRST (Before calling any other rbw command)
    # Since RBW_PROFILE is exported, rbw will use the new config dir
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # Optional: Identity URL if provided in config.conf
    if [[ -n "${CRED_IDENTITY_URL}" ]]; then
        rbw config set identity_url "${CRED_IDENTITY_URL}"
    fi

    # Register the device - this actually performs the login
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)
    
    output --info "Registering device with server: ${base_url:-api.bitwarden.com} (credentials profile)..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed! Please check your credentials and Base URL."
        # Cleanup failed config to allow retry
        rm -f "$config_file"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'credentials' completed successfully."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking (Credentials Profile)
# Rapidly checks if the secondary profile is unlocked.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    # Verify installation
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # CRITICAL: Ensure setup is done BEFORE any other rbw call
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast status check for current profile
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Unlock via profile-specific pass entry
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Update local cache for this profile
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'key' module.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and interactive auto-configuration.
# This file is entirely self-contained.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    local cmd="$1"
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN:-vaultwarden}"
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        # We don't print error here to avoid double-output during setup
        return 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures rbw is configured. Prompts for missing data (Email, Base URL).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    local config_dir="$HOME/.config/rbw"
    local config_file="${config_dir}/config.json"
    
    # Return immediately if config already exists
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --section "Setup: Bitwarden 'key' Profile"
    output --info "Configuration is missing. Please provide the following details."

    # Pre-create directory so config set commands don't fail silently
    mkdir -p "$config_dir"

    # Use variables from config.conf if available, otherwise prompt interactivly
    local email="${KEY_EMAIL}"
    local base_url="${KEY_BASE_URL}"

    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email (main account):" @email
    fi

    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (e.g. https://vault.yourserver.com):" @base_url
    fi

    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; exit 1; }

    # Set basic configuration BEFORE calling any command that triggers the agent
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # Retrieve password for registration
    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass store for profile: default."
        # Cleanup to allow fresh retry
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --info "Registering device with server: ${base_url:-api.bitwarden.com}..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed! Please check your credentials and server URL."
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'key' completed successfully."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and performs unlocking if required.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # Ensure setup is valid before proceeding
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Check if currently unlocked
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Automate unlocking via expect
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Ensure cache is synced
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Credentials ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'credentials' module.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and interactive auto-configuration
# for the secondary account profile.

# Force rbw to use a dedicated profile for the secondary credentials account.
export RBW_PROFILE="credentials"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    local cmd="$1"
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_CREDENTIALS:-vaultwarden-credentials}"
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        return 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Credentials Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures the credentials profile is configured. Prompts for missing data.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    local config_dir="$HOME/.config/rbw-credentials"
    local config_file="${config_dir}/config.json"
    
    # Return immediately if config already exists
    [[ -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    output --section "Setup: Bitwarden 'credentials' Profile"
    output --info "Configuration is missing. Please provide the following details."

    # Pre-create profile directory
    mkdir -p "$config_dir"

    # Use variables from config.conf if available, otherwise prompt interactivly
    local email="${CRED_EMAIL}"
    local base_url="${CRED_BASE_URL}"

    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email (credentials account):" @email
    fi

    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (e.g. https://vault.yourserver.com):" @base_url
    fi

    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; exit 1; }

    # Set basic configuration BEFORE calling any command that triggers the agent
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # Retrieve password for registration
    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass store for entry: ${CMD_PASS_CREDENTIALS:-vaultwarden-credentials}."
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --info "Registering device with server: ${base_url:-api.bitwarden.com}..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed! Please check your credentials and server URL."
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'credentials' completed successfully."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking (Credentials Profile)
# Rapidly checks if the secondary profile is unlocked.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # CRITICAL: Ensure setup is done BEFORE any other rbw call
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast status check for current profile
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Unlock via profile-specific pass entry
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Sync local cache
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: key
# Delegates the entire argument parsing and autocompletion to 'rbw'.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Check if config exists. If not, EXIT SILENTLY.
    # This prevents background rbw calls from triggering the login prompt
    # while the user is still typing the command.
    local config_file="$HOME/.config/rbw/config.json"
    [[ ! -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    # Ensure rbw is unlocked only if config is already valid
    _unlock_rbw

    # Delegate completion to rbw
    arg_wrap "rbw"
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: credentials
# Delegates parsing and autocompletion to 'rbw' under the credentials profile.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Check if profile config exists. If not, EXIT SILENTLY.
    # This stops background rbw calls until the user runs the setup via main command.
    local config_file="$HOME/.config/rbw-credentials/config.json"
    [[ ! -f "$config_file" ]] && return 0

    # Only attempt to unlock if configuration is present
    _unlock_rbw

    # Inherit native rbw completion for the specific profile
    arg_wrap "rbw"
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'key' module.
# Manages rbw (Bitwarden Rust CLI) unlocking and interactive auto-configuration.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Command Check
# Verifies that a required command exists before proceeding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _check_cmd() {
    local cmd="$1"
    if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
        output --error "Error: The required command '$cmd' is not installed."
        exit 1 
    fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Determine the pass entry name from config or use current variable
    local cmd_pass="${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN}"
    
    # If still empty, use default
    [[ -z "$cmd_pass" ]] && cmd_pass="vaultwarden"

    # Ensure pinentry uses the current TTY
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    # Get password from pass store
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        return 1
    fi
    
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Interactive Auto-Configuration
# Ensures rbw is configured correctly.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _ensure_rbw_setup() {
    local config_dir="$HOME/.config/rbw"
    local config_file="${config_dir}/config.json"
    
    # Check if config exists AND contains an email address
    if [[ -f "$config_file" ]]; then
        if grep -q "email" "$config_file"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    output --section "Setup: Bitwarden 'key' (Main Account)"
    output --info "No valid configuration found. Let's set it up now."

    # Pre-create directory
    mkdir -p "$config_dir"

    # 1. Ask for Email
    local email="${KEY_EMAIL}"
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter your Bitwarden Email:" @email
    fi
    [[ -z "$email" ]] && { output --error "Email is required."; rm -rf "$config_dir"; exit 1; }

    # 2. Ask for Base URL
    local base_url="${KEY_BASE_URL}"
    if [[ -z "$base_url" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter Vaultwarden Base URL (leave empty for Bitwarden Cloud):" @base_url
    fi

    # 3. Ask for Pass Entry Name
    if [[ -z "${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN}" ]]; then
        lx input --prompt "Enter the name of your password in 'pass' (e.g. vaultwarden):" @CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN
    fi
    [[ -z "${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN}" ]] && CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN="vaultwarden"

    # APPLY CONFIG
    rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$base_url" ]]; then
        rbw config set base_url "$base_url"
    fi

    # 4. Perform Registration
    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Could not find password in pass under: ${CMD_PASS_VAULTWARDEN}"
        output --info "Please make sure the entry exists in your pass store."
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --info "Registering device with server..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed! Check your credentials and Base URL."
        rm -rf "$config_dir"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    output --ok "Setup for 'key' completed."
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    _check_cmd rbw
    
    # Start setup if needed
    _ensure_rbw_setup
    
    # Fast status check
    if rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    local vault_pass
    if ! vault_pass=$(_get_master_password); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass store."
        output --warn "Try running 'lpex key' to re-trigger setup if the pass entry changed."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Automate unlocking via expect
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

    fi

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Extension Global Library: Key ---
# Provides global helper functions utilized by the 'key' module.
# Deals exclusively with 'rbw' (Bitwarden Rust CLI) and unlocking via 'pass'.
# Redirects rbw configuration to the extension's data directory.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Wrapper
# Executes rbw with a redirected configuration path to ensure isolation.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _rbw() {
    # Define the isolated config path based on the extension's data directory
    local rbw_config_path="${PATH_EXTENSION_DATA}/config"
    
    # Ensure the directory exists
    mkdir -p "$rbw_config_path"
    
    # Execute rbw with the redirected XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$rbw_config_path" command rbw "$@"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: Master Password Retrieval
# Safely retrieves the vault password from 'pass' via GPG.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _get_master_password() {
    # Use the pass entry name from configuration or fallback to 'vaultwarden'
    local cmd_pass="${KEY_PASS_ENTRY:-vaultwarden}"

    # Explicitly set GPG_TTY for pinentry popups
    export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
    
    local vault_pass
    # Retrieve the password from the pass store
    if ! vault_pass=$(pass show "$cmd_pass" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); then
        output --error "Failed to retrieve password from pass for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Validate the result
    if [[ -z "$vault_pass" ]]; then
        output --error "Pass returned an empty password for '$cmd_pass'." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Return the password
    echo "$vault_pass"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature: RBW Unlocking
# Rapidly checks if rbw is unlocked and performs unlocking if required.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function _unlock_rbw() {
    # Check if rbw is already unlocked using our isolated wrapper
    if _rbw unlocked &> /dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Retrieve the master password
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    # Use expect to automate the unlocking process for the isolated instance
    expect <<EOF &> /dev/null
log_user 0
spawn XDG_CONFIG_HOME="${PATH_EXTENSION_DATA}/config" rbw unlock
expect "Master Password:"
send "${vault_pass}\r"
expect eof
EOF
    
    # Sync the local database after unlocking
    _rbw sync &> /dev/null
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Arguments Definition ---
# Module: key init
# Defines parameters for initializing the Bitwarden account.
# ==============================================================================

function arguments() {
    # Request the email address
    arg_value @email \
        --description "Bitwarden account email" \
        --ask

    # Request the Vaultwarden server URL
    arg_value @url \
        --description "Vaultwarden server URL (e.g., https://vault.example.com)" \
        --ask

    # Request the name of the password in the local 'pass' store
    arg_value @pass-entry \
        --description "Name of the password entry in 'pass' (default: vaultwarden)" \
        --ask
}

#!/bin/bash
# ==============================================================================
# --- Main Execution ---
# Module: key init
# Configures rbw and registers the device using isolated configuration.
# ==============================================================================

function extension_start() {
    # Store provided arguments into local variables
    local email="${ARG_EMAIL:-}"
    local url="${ARG_URL:-}"
    local pentry="${ARG_PASS_ENTRY:-vaultwarden}"

    # Validation: email is required
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        output --error "Initialization failed: Email is required."
        exit 1
    fi

    output --info "Initializing Bitwarden 'key' profile..."

    # Persist the configuration values to the extension's config.conf
    # This allows other subcommands to access the 'pass' entry name later.
    lx db --file "config.conf" --table "config" --insert --data "KEY_EMAIL" "$email" "KEY_BASE_URL" "$url" "KEY_PASS_ENTRY" "$pentry" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Also set as shell variables for the current session setup
    KEY_EMAIL="$email"
    KEY_BASE_URL="$url"
    KEY_PASS_ENTRY="$pentry"

    # Configure rbw settings using our isolated wrapper
    output --info "Setting up rbw configuration..."
    _rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$url" ]]; then
        _rbw config set base_url "$url"
    fi

    # Retrieve the master password from 'pass'
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    # Perform registration with the server
    output --info "Registering device with server..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | _rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed. Please check your credentials and URL."
        exit 1
    fi

    output --ok "Bitwarden 'key' profile successfully initialized."
}

function extension_start() {
    # Localize provided arguments
    local email="${ARG_EMAIL:-}"
    local url="${ARG_URL:-}"
    local pentry="${ARG_PASS_ENTRY:-vaultwarden-credentials}"

    # Validation
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        output --error "Initialization failed: Email is required."
        exit 1

    output --info "Initializing Bitwarden 'credentials' profile..."

    # Persist the configuration values to the local credentials config.conf
    lx db --file "config.conf" --table "config" --insert --data "CRED_EMAIL" "$email" "CRED_BASE_URL" "$url" "CRED_PASS_ENTRY" "$pentry" 2>/dev/null || true

    CRED_EMAIL="$email"
    CRED_BASE_URL="$url"
    CRED_PASS_ENTRY="$pentry"

    # Configure the isolated rbw instance
    output --info "Setting up rbw configuration..."
    _rbw config set email "$email"
    if [[ -n "$url" ]]; then
        _rbw config set base_url "$url"
    fi

    # Retrieve the password from pass
    local vault_pass
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password)

    # Perform registration
    output --info "Registering device with server..."
    if ! printf "%s" "$vault_pass" | _rbw register; then
        output --error "Registration failed. Please check your credentials and URL."
        exit 1
    fi

    output --ok "Bitwarden 'credentials' profile successfully initialized."
}

    # This allows other subcommands to access the 'pass' entry name later.
    lx db --file "config.conf" --table "config" --insert --data "KEY_EMAIL" "$email" "KEY_BASE_URL" "$url" "KEY_PASS_ENTRY" "$pentry" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Note: These are capitalized to match typical config variable conventions
    KEY_EMAIL="$email"
    KEY_BASE_URL="$url"
    KEY_PASS_ENTRY="$pentry"

    if [[ -n "$url" ]]; then
        _rbw config set base_url "$url"
    fi

    # Retrieve the master password from 'pass'
    local vault_pass
    # We pass the entry name explicitly to the helper
    vault_pass=$(_get_master_password "$pentry")

    # Perform registration with the server
    output --info "Registering device with server: ${url:-api.bitwarden.com}..."

function extension_start() {
    # Store provided arguments into local variables
    local email="${ARG_EMAIL:-}"
    local url="${ARG_URL:-}"
    local pentry="${ARG_PASS_ENTRY:-}"

    # Validation: email is required
    if [[ -z "$email" ]]; then
        output --error "Initialization failed: Email is required."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Set default for pass entry if not provided
    [[ -z "$pentry" ]] && pentry="vaultwarden"

    if [[ -n "$url" ]] && [[ "$url" != http* ]]; then
        output --warn "URL missing protocol. Assuming https://$url"
        url="https://$url"
    fi

    output --info "Initializing Bitwarden 'key' profile..."

    # Persist the configuration values to the extension's config.conf
    lx db --file "config.conf" --table "config" --insert --data "KEY_EMAIL" "$email" "KEY_BASE_URL" "$url" "KEY_PASS_ENTRY" "$pentry" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Inject variables for current session
    KEY_EMAIL="$email"
    KEY_BASE_URL="$url"
    KEY_PASS_ENTRY="$pentry"

    # Configure rbw settings using our isolated wrapper
    output --info "Setting up rbw configuration..."
    _rbw config set email "$email"
